since.title: BLAST IGNITION
since.text: BLAST IGNITION (GRIND startup): with GRIND_NATIVE=1 the start screen is a static SYSTEM WAKE during the firmware's initialisation, followed by a 400 ms moving presentation (ignition, attack, ready) on the first normal screen. Any button, key or encoder step, a dialog, a message, SAFE START, a persistent-data note, calibration or update traffic ends it at once and the normal action happens as usual; the boot's own LOADED note keeps its full lifetime. It runs once per power-on and stores nothing. The GRIND_NATIVE=0 start screen is unchanged. The web simulator can show the scene with ?boot=1 (a scene preview, not a timing measurement). See docs/grind/acceptance.md.

since.title: GRIND style browser
since.text: GRIND style browser: a fifth GRIND page (STYLE, BANK, APPLY) shows any of the 23 styles as eight roles over a 16-step bank before anything changes; APPLY is a normal STYLE turn, leaving the page cancels. See docs/grind/live-pages.md.

since.title: VARY
since.text: VARY (GRIND, page 3): a deterministic velocity swing per generated hit (up to +-8), 0 = unchanged sound. Not stored.

since.title: LIVE page
since.text: LIVE page (GRIND): SINK (master lowpass), SWELL (more delay/reverb send) and CUT (performance stop); at 0 the sound is bit-identical to before. Not stored.

since.title: Fix
since.text: Fix: a GRIND runtime reset started from the invalid style id 0; it starts from style 1's config now.

since.title: 7/4 Mathcore
since.text: 7/4 Mathcore (GRIND): the STYLE list has a 23rd entry, MATH: Technical on a seven-quarter bar (3+2+2), LEN 28 at 1/16 (56 at 1/32, 14 at 1/8; two bars at 1/16 fit as 56). Kick and its accent on steps 1, 13, 21, snare on 9, 17, 25, crash on the downbeat, ride on every second step. Only Technical has a 7/4 rule: other styles on a 7/4 grid are refused (GM_UNSUPPORTED). The core's style ids, the saved bytes and the golden patterns are unchanged; an older firmware reads the saved entry as STYLE 1. A pattern staged for the end waits for step 28.

since.title: HARDWARE CALIBRATION can be left,
since.text: HARDWARE CALIBRATION can be left, and the menu can reset to the defaults: while a key is asked for, tap it to teach it, or hold it for 1.5 s to cancel; while a knob is asked for, any key cancels (the 30 s without input still gives up). A cancelled calibration keeps the old table (SETUP CANCELLED). The new menu row RESET TO DEFAULT (OCT+ asks, OCT+ again within about 1.5 s acts) puts COLOR, SPEAKER EQ, USB LEVEL, USB AUDIO, PERFORM, ZOOM, ACCEL, BACKLIGHT, the mute timing, MIDI THRU, SOLO, QUANT, the GRIND style and WHEN and the panel table back to what a first start has. Projects, presets, samples and the Bluetooth device and mode are not touched. The menu has twelve rows now (a 13 px pitch).

since.title: tools/songs_pattern.py
since.text: tools/songs_pattern.py: drum patterns from song excerpts (a JSON of songs with a tempo map and drum notes). show prints a 4-bar window as the eight GRIND roles, compare sets each song against the 22 styles' golden patterns (nearest styles and role densities), send writes the window to the FM-1's loaded pattern over USB-MIDI (steps, accents, each step's NUDGE for what the 16th grid cannot hold, LEN 64 / 16th, optionally the tempo; not saved unless --save). Tested on made-up songs and against the editor's mock FM-1. The band's song excerpts are in assets/songs/ (reference material, not part of any build; see its README).

since.title: GRIND pages
since.text: GRIND pages (builds with GRIND_NATIVE=1 only; not in the default image): press ARP again after GRIDS for two pages, STYLE AGGR DENS CHAOS and HUMAN MUT WHEN. STYLE picks one of 22 rhythm styles and brings its factory controls; the other knobs re-generate the pattern of all eight tracks from them, MUT rolls a new variation. While the sequencer plays, WHEN END waits for the end of the longest pattern and WHEN STEP for the next step, then every track restarts from its first step together; stopped, the pattern changes at once. A step, LEN, DIV, SWG or SRC you edit while a change waits wins: the waiting change is dropped ("NOT APPLIED"). A running song refuses ("STOP THE SONG"). The generator writes kick, snare, hi-hat, ride, crash, china and two toms to tracks 1 to 8, so GRIND page 2 has a KIT action: ROLE gives the eight tracks those sounds (one detent asks, a second within about a second and a half acts; stopped only; levels, pans, FX sends and patterns stay; the cymbal and tom offsets are starting points, not tuned by ear). STYLE and WHEN are remembered with the device settings, not in a project, and nothing about the project format changes: they use palette bits 18 to 23 of the settings record, which an older firmware ignores (the controls come back as the style's factory values). GRIND page 3 has KEEP, UNDO and FREE. KEEP marks steps of the selected track that a new pattern must leave as they are, rests included: hold a step key in STEPS (ENV) on any GRIND page to toggle one (STEP 3 KEPT; the step itself is not touched), or turn the KEEP knob up to keep the whole track and down to free it; FREE frees every track. A change whose grid the kept steps do not fit says KEEP DOES NOT FIT and applies nothing. KEEPs are not stored and go when another pattern is loaded or cued. UNDO takes the tracks back to what they were before the last GRIND change; UNDO again goes forward (steps and lengths; not your own edits made since).

since.title: GRIND in the USB web editor
since.text: GRIND in the USB web editor: compatible firmware exposes the GRIND tab for style, generation controls, the role kit, step and track KEEP, and undo/redo. The tab shows when a pattern is waiting for a playback boundary. Save the loaded project with Patterns → Save on FM-1 while stopped. Use SAVE on the device to choose a slot when none is loaded. Earlier firmware keeps its existing editor tabs.

notes.title: Newer FM-1s save again
notes.text: Newer FM-1s save again: FM-1s sold recently come with a different flash chip of the same size. Hortator now recognises it, so projects, presets and settings are saved on these units instead of staying in memory with a flash error.
